cues.a: In 64 CE, Rome caught fire.
cues.b: 公元64年，罗马烧了起来。

cues.a: The flames raced from the low streets up the hillsides,
cues.b: 大火顺着低处的街巷往山坡上窜，

cues.a: and families ran for their lives.
cues.b: 满城的人拖家带口，拼命往外逃。

cues.a: Who would have thought that this city,
cues.b: 谁能想到，

cues.a: home to more than 2.7 million people today,
cues.b: 这座今天住着270多万人的城市，

cues.a: began as a few clusters of thatched huts by the River Tiber?
cues.b: 最早，只是台伯河边的几片茅草屋。

cues.a: The River Tiber runs between a group of hills in central Italy,
cues.b: 台伯河穿过意大利中部的几座山丘，

cues.a: then on to the Mediterranean Sea.
cues.b: 一路流进地中海。

cues.a: By the 8th century BCE, people were living on these slopes.
cues.b: 公元前8世纪，这些山坡上已经有了人家。

cues.a: Their huts stood in small clusters with open ground between them;
cues.b: 茅屋三五成群，中间隔着大片荒地；

cues.a: even the Palatine Hill, where emperors would
cues.b: 就连后来建起皇宫的帕拉蒂尼山，

cues.a: later build their palaces, had only thatched huts.
cues.b: 那时也只有草房。

cues.a: In the river lay a small island, the easiest place to cross.
cues.b: 河心有一座小岛，是渡河最省力的地方。

cues.a: Goods brought up from the coast were unloaded here,
cues.b: 海边运来的货物在这里卸船，

cues.a: and travellers crossed here on their way north and south.
cues.b: 南来北往的行人从这里过河。

cues.a: The first Rome grew up at this crossing,
cues.b: 最早的罗马，

cues.a: where the river met the road.
cues.b: 就长在这个水陆交汇的渡口旁。

cues.a: The Romans' own legend says that in 753 BCE Romulus founded
cues.b: 按罗马人自己的传说，公元前753年，

cues.a: a city here and became its king. The name Rome comes from him.
cues.b: 罗慕路斯在这里筑城称王，“罗马”这个名字，就来自他。

cues.a: In 509 BCE the Romans drove out
cues.b: 公元前509年，罗马人赶走最后一位国王，

cues.a: their last king and founded a republic.
cues.b: 建立共和国。

cues.a: Affairs of state were decided by the Senate,
cues.b: 国家大事交给元老院、

cues.a: the citizens' assemblies and elected officials,
cues.b: 公民大会和选出来的官员共同决定，

cues.a: and the officials had to give up their power when their term ended.
cues.b: 官员任期一到就得交权。

cues.a: From then on, no single man ruled Rome.
cues.b: 从那以后，罗马不再由一个人说了算。

cues.a: Over the next few centuries, Rome's armies conquered the Italian
cues.b: 接下来的几百年里，罗马军队先打下意大利半岛，

cues.a: peninsula, then reached out across the Mediterranean.
cues.b: 又把势力伸向整个地中海。

cues.a: By the 2nd century BCE,
cues.b: 到公元前2世纪，台伯河边的这座城，

cues.a: the city on the Tiber ruled a vast territory.
cues.b: 已经统治着一大片疆域。

cues.a: Grain, tribute and the spoils of war flowed in from far away; the city
cues.b: 远方的粮食、贡赋和战利品运进城里，

cues.a: spread outward ring by ring, and its public squares grew grander.
cues.b: 城区一圈圈向外长，广场也越修越大。

cues.a: But as the wars were fought further and further away,
cues.b: 但仗越打越远，

cues.a: generals came to have armies loyal to them alone,
cues.b: 将军们手里有了只听自己号令的军队，

cues.a: and with those armies, the means to challenge the Senate.
cues.b: 也就有了跟元老院较量的本钱。

cues.a: The most famous of these generals was Julius Caesar.
cues.b: 凯撒是其中最有名的一个。

cues.a: He spent 8 years fighting in Gaul, roughly today's France,
cues.b: 他在高卢，也就是今天的法国一带，

cues.a: and came back with a great army that answered to him.
cues.b: 打了8年仗，带回一支忠于他的大军。

cues.a: In 49 BCE Caesar led his troops across the Rubicon River into Italy.
cues.b: 公元前49年，凯撒率军越过卢比孔河，进入意大利。

cues.a: Civil war began:
cues.b: 内战开始了，罗马人打罗马人，

cues.a: Romans fought Romans over who would rule the state.
cues.b: 争的是谁来统治这个国家。

cues.a: Caesar won, and was made dictator for life,
cues.b: 凯撒赢了内战，

cues.a: with all power in his hands.
cues.b: 当上终身独裁官，大权集于一身。

cues.a: He was already remaking the city: a new square carried his name.
cues.b: 他已经在改造这座城：一座以他命名的新广场落成了。

cues.a: A group of senators decided that to save the Republic,
cues.b: 一批元老暗下决心：

cues.a: Caesar had to die.
cues.b: 要想保住共和，凯撒必须死。

cues.a: On 15 March 44 BCE, the Senate met in a hall built by Pompey.
cues.b: 公元前44年3月15日，元老院在庞培议事厅开会。

cues.a: As soon as Caesar sat down,
cues.b: 凯撒刚坐下，刺客就围了上来，

cues.a: the assassins closed in and stabbed him to death.
cues.b: 用刀把他刺死在会场里。

cues.a: But killing Caesar did not save the Republic.
cues.b: 但刺死凯撒，并没有救回共和国。

cues.a: Civil war went on for more than 10 years,
cues.b: 罗马又打了10多年内战，

cues.a: until Caesar's adopted son Octavian came out the winner.
cues.b: 最后的赢家是凯撒的养子屋大维。

cues.a: In 27 BCE the Senate gave him the title Augustus.
cues.b: 公元前27年，元老院献给他“奥古斯都”的尊号——

cues.a: The Republic was over, and Rome had its first emperor.
cues.b: 罗马告别了共和，有了第一位皇帝。

cues.a: After the civil wars, Augustus set about rebuilding the capital:
cues.b: 内战结束后，奥古斯都着手整修首都，

cues.a: he restored old temples and gave the citizens new public squares.
cues.b: 修复旧神庙，给市民建新广场。

cues.a: He liked to boast that he had found
cues.b: 他曾得意地说，自己接手的是一座砖头城，

cues.a: a city of brick and left a city of marble.
cues.b: 留下的是一座大理石城。

cues.a: But the marble went into temples and squares; ordinary Romans still
cues.b: 可大理石多用在神庙和广场上，

cues.a: crowded into tall blocks of rented rooms along narrow streets.
cues.b: 普通市民仍挤在窄巷里的多层出租楼中。

cues.a: By then Rome may have held close to 1 million people,
cues.b: 那时的罗马，可能已住着近100万人。

cues.a: far more than the farmland around it could feed.
cues.b: 城外的田地养不活这么多人，

cues.a: Grain was shipped from North Africa and Egypt
cues.b: 粮食要从北非和埃及装船，

cues.a: across the Mediterranean,
cues.b: 渡过地中海，

cues.a: then brought up the Tiber into the city.
cues.b: 再沿台伯河运进城。

cues.a: If the grain ships were a few days late, the city went hungry.
cues.b: 粮船晚到几天，城里就要挨饿。

cues.a: In 51 CE, during a shortage, Rome had only 15 days of food left,
cues.b: 公元51年闹粮荒，存粮只够吃15天，

cues.a: and an angry crowd surrounded the emperor Claudius.
cues.b: 愤怒的市民围住了皇帝克劳狄乌斯。

cues.a: Besides hunger, this city of tall buildings
cues.b: 除了饥荒，这座挤满高楼窄巷的城还怕一样东西：

cues.a: and narrow streets feared one more thing: fire.
cues.b: 火。

cues.a: In 64 CE, under the emperor Nero, a fire broke out in shops
cues.b: 公元64年，尼禄在位时，

cues.a: beside the Circus Maximus, the great chariot-racing track.
cues.b: 大赛车场边的店铺起了火。

cues.a: Driven by the wind, it swept along the narrow streets of the valley
cues.b: 火借着风，顺着低处的窄街一路烧上山坡。

cues.a: and up the hills. People fled, helping the old and carrying the young;
cues.b: 逃难的人扶老携幼，

cues.a: those in front were still looking for a way out while those
cues.b: 前面的还没找到出路，后面的又涌了上来。

cues.a: behind pushed forward. On the 6th day, people tore down a whole
cues.b: 烧到第6天，人们拆掉一大片房子，

cues.a: stretch of houses to make a firebreak, and the fire was stopped.
cues.b: 空出一道隔火带，才把火挡住；

cues.a: Soon it broke out again and burned still more of the city.
cues.b: 没过多久，火又烧起来，烧掉了更多街区。

cues.a: Legend says that while Rome burned, Nero played his lyre and sang.
cues.b: 传说，罗马燃烧时，尼禄在高处弹琴唱歌。

cues.a: No one knows for certain how the fire started. What Nero did next
cues.b: 火到底是怎么烧起来的，至今没人说得清；

cues.a: showed whose interests came first: in the burned-out heart of the city
cues.b: 尼禄接下来做的事，却让人看清了他的私心：

cues.a: he took a huge stretch of land for his Golden House and its gardens,
cues.b: 他在烧光的城中心圈下一大片地，

cues.a: and dug an artificial lake in the valley.
cues.b: 修起他的金宫和园林，还在谷底挖了一个人工湖。

cues.a: Streets where families had lived became one man's private park.
cues.b: 原来住满人家的街坊，成了皇帝一个人的园子。

cues.a: After Nero's death,
cues.b: 尼禄死后，

cues.a: the emperor Vespasian gave the land back to the people of Rome.
cues.b: 皇帝维斯帕先把这片地还给了罗马市民：

cues.a: He drained the lake
cues.b: 排干湖水，

cues.a: and began building a great arena on the spot.
cues.b: 在原地建一座大竞技场。

cues.a: In 80 CE his son, the emperor Titus, opened it.
cues.b: 公元80年，他的儿子提图斯皇帝为它揭幕。

cues.a: Where an emperor had kept a private lake,
cues.b: 皇帝独享的湖面，

cues.a: there were now seats for about 50,000 people.
cues.b: 变成了约5万人的看台。

cues.a: This is the Colosseum.
cues.b: 这就是罗马斗兽场。

cues.a: By the early 2nd century, under the emperor Trajan,
cues.b: 到了2世纪初的图拉真皇帝时，

cues.a: the empire reached its greatest size.
cues.b: 帝国的疆域达到最大。

cues.a: In the capital, the wealth of generations of conquest was turned
cues.b: 一代代征服带回的财富，

cues.a: into temples, baths and public squares, one after another.
cues.b: 在首都变成了一座又一座神庙、浴场和广场。

cues.a: Yet the empire's golden age could not last forever.
cues.b: 然而，帝国的黄金时代终有落幕的时候。

cues.a: By 271, invaders from the north were closing in on Italy.
cues.b: 公元271年，北方的入侵者已经逼近意大利。

cues.a: Rome had long since spread beyond its old walls,
cues.b: 罗马城区早就漫出了几百年前的旧城墙，

cues.a: built centuries before, and the emperor Aurelian ordered
cues.b: 皇帝奥勒良下令，

cues.a: a new wall to be raised around the whole city in haste.
cues.b: 绕着整座城抢修一道新墙。

cues.a: In 275 the Aurelian Wall, about 19 km long, was complete.
cues.b: 4年后，约19公里长的奥勒良城墙合拢。

cues.a: By now the emperors rarely lived in Rome.
cues.b: 可这时的皇帝，已经很少住在罗马。

cues.a: In 330 Constantine the Great founded a new capital in the east,
cues.b: 330年，君士坦丁大帝在东方建立新都君士坦丁堡，

cues.a: Constantinople, today's Istanbul.
cues.b: 也就是今天的伊斯坦布尔。

cues.a: Also in Constantine's time,
cues.b: 也是在君士坦丁的时代，台伯河西岸、

cues.a: the first St Peter's Basilica was built across the Tiber,
cues.b: 相传安葬着耶稣门徒彼得的地方，

cues.a: on the spot where Jesus's disciple Peter was said to be buried.
cues.b: 建起了最早的圣彼得大教堂。

cues.a: From then on,
cues.b: 此后，

cues.a: pilgrims came to Rome from every direction to visit this tomb.
cues.b: 四面八方的朝圣者为这座墓来到罗马。

cues.a: Later the empire split into an eastern and a western half,
cues.b: 后来，帝国分成东西两半，

cues.a: each with its own emperor.
cues.b: 各有一位皇帝。

cues.a: In 402 the western emperor moved his court to Ravenna,
which was easier to defend.
cues.b: 西罗马皇帝把朝廷搬到了更易防守的拉文纳。

cues.a: Rome's walls were raised higher.
cues.b: 罗马的城墙又加高了一截。

cues.a: Only 6 years later, in 408, the Visigothic king Alaric cut
cues.b: 仅仅6年后，408年，西哥特国王阿拉里克

cues.a: off the route that brought grain from the port into the city.
cues.b: 带兵截断了从海港运粮进城的路。

cues.a: Rations were cut again and again,
cues.b: 城里的口粮一减再减，

cues.a: and Rome had to pay a ransom to make him withdraw.
cues.b: 罗马只好交出赎金，换他退兵。

cues.a: In the summer of 410 he came back,
cues.b: 410年夏天，他又带兵回来，

cues.a: and this time his army broke through the gates and sacked the city.
cues.b: 这一次攻进了城门，洗劫了罗马。

cues.a: It was the first time in 800 years
cues.b: 这是800年来，

cues.a: that a foreign enemy had taken Rome.
cues.b: 罗马第一次被外敌攻破。

cues.a: Far away, the Christian scholar Jerome heard the news and wrote:
cues.b: 消息传到远方，基督教学者哲罗姆在信中写道：

cues.a: "The city which had taken the whole world was itself taken."
cues.b: “那座征服了整个世界的城，自己竟被征服了。”

cues.a: The Western Roman Empire held on for a few more decades.
cues.b: 西罗马帝国又勉强撑了几十年。

cues.a: In 476 the army commander Odoacer deposed the last
cues.b: 476年，军队统帅奥多亚塞废黜了西罗马的末代皇帝，

cues.a: western emperor and took Italy for himself.
cues.b: 自己掌握了意大利。

cues.a: As it happened, the young emperor was named Romulus Augustus:
cues.b: 巧的是，这位年轻皇帝的名字叫“罗慕路斯·奥古斯都”

cues.a: Romulus, the city's founder, and Augustus, its first emperor.
cues.b: ——前半截是建城的始祖，后半截是第一位皇帝。

cues.a: The Western Empire ended with that name.
cues.b: 西罗马帝国，就结束在这个名字上。

cues.a: In the east, the Roman Empire lived on,
cues.b: 东边的罗马帝国还在，

cues.a: with its capital at Constantinople.
cues.b: 都城是君士坦丁堡。

cues.a: In 493 the king of the Ostrogoths took Italy from Odoacer,
cues.b: 493年，东哥特国王从奥多亚塞手里夺下意大利，

cues.a: and Rome became a city of the Ostrogothic kingdom.
cues.b: 罗马成了东哥特王国里的一座城。

cues.a: In the 6th century the eastern emperor Justinian set out
cues.b: 到了6世纪，东罗马皇帝查士丁尼决心收回意大利，

cues.a: to win Italy back and sent his general Belisarius west.
cues.b: 派大将贝利撒留西征。

cues.a: Belisarius entered Rome in 536; the next year
cues.b: 536年，贝利撒留进了罗马；

cues.a: the Ostrogothic army returned and laid siege to the city.
cues.b: 次年，东哥特大军杀了回来，把城围住。

cues.a: The Goths cut the aqueducts.
cues.b: 东哥特人切断了引水渠。

cues.a: The mills on the Janiculum Hill were driven by aqueduct water,
cues.b: 贾尼科洛山上的磨坊靠渠水推动，

cues.a: and with the water gone, they stopped.
cues.b: 水一断，磨就停了。

cues.a: Without the mills, grain could not be ground into flour,
cues.b: 粮食磨不成面粉，

cues.a: and there was no bread.
cues.b: 就做不成面包。

cues.a: Belisarius found a way:
